A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EXPO and contain readable methods, equations, experimental figures, references, and complete appendices. Relocated material can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original online and offline-to-online reinforcement-learning experiments on 12 tasks, plus component and dataset-quality ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds entropy-variant, offline-data-retention, and hyperparameter studies, including Appendix A.

M1.justification: v3 adds an optional entropy-backup variant in Section 4.3, introducing softmax selection over candidate actions and entropy-regularized OTF objectives. This substantially extends v1's hard-max action extraction and edit-policy entropy regularization, although the original EXPO construction remains.

E1.justification: The same 12 tasks across Antmaze, Adroit, Robomimic, and MimicGen remain. Appendix A.1 adds a limited training-input scenario on Lift and Can: fine-tuning a pretrained policy without retaining its original offline dataset.

E2.justification: DIPO is added to the online comparison in v3 Figure 3. Appendix A.1 also evaluates Cal-QL pretraining followed by SAC fine-tuning against EXPO without retained offline data. The original main offline-to-online comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: Table 1 changes Antmaze's edit scale from 0 to 0.05 in both settings. The Square dataset-size study changes its evaluation endpoint from 500k to 1M environment steps. New ablations introduce matched-count warm-start rollouts and controlled sample-count/edit-scale variations. These are reported setting changes; they do not establish which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: Figure 7 compares entropy and standard EXPO across dataset quality, while Appendix A tests removal of retained offline data and sensitivity to action-sample count and edit scale. The original TD-backup and action-edit ablation plots are retained as Figures 5–6.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three seeds with minimum/maximum error bars, and both dataset-size plots report averaging over three seeds. No increased run count, new confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported. v3's smoothing disclosure does not establish a changed uncertainty estimator.

E6.justification: v3 adds DIPO results and substantial new ablation outcomes. Figure 7 reports near-perfect entropy-variant performance from a prior with below 10% imitation performance; Figure 8 reports successful fine-tuning without retained offline data, unlike its Cal-QL/SAC comparator. Figures 9–10 add sensitivity results. The revised Square study uses 1M rather than 500k steps, precluding a same-setting improvement claim.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 adds mathematical formulations for entropy-regularized targets and objectives in Equations 4–5 and defines a Q-weighted soft sampling distribution. Existing mathematical foundations remain; no new theorem, convergence guarantee, or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statement, and conclusion retain the central claims: stable, policy-agnostic expressive-policy fine-tuning and approximately 2–3x sample-efficiency improvement across 12 tasks in four domains. The added studies do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v3 qualifies the earlier dependence on offline-data quality by attributing improved weak-prior performance to soft sampling and entropy-driven exploration. Appendix A interprets pretrained policies as sufficient priors without retaining their datasets and explains edit-scale sensitivity. The computational-cost and uninformed-prior limitations remain; the earlier rationale for disabling Antmaze edits is removed.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link and reproducibility statement. Appendix B newly documents running-average smoothing with windows of three or five and unsmoothed shaded regions; Appendix A specifies how warm-start rollout counts are chosen. Most architecture, optimizer, dataset-composition, and evaluation details are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 refocuses the prior-data discussion and clarifies relationships to EMAQ/MADE and softmax action selection. References supporting MADE, maximum-entropy RL, and DIPO are added, while several general sample-efficiency and architecture references are removed. The overall research positioning remains.

P1.justification: v3 makes focused related-work and explanatory rewrites, moves detailed baseline descriptions to Appendix C, reorganizes the appendices, and adds acknowledgments and a reproducibility statement. Most introductory, algorithmic, experimental, and concluding prose remains closely matched.

P2.justification: The visual organization is substantially revised: three new analysis figures are added, the dataset-quality plot gains an entropy comparison and rescales its horizontal axis, Figure 2 becomes a wrapped sidebar, and the environment montage moves to the appendix. Existing figures and tables are redistributed within the conference layout.

improvement.justification: The additional comparator and targeted ablations strengthen evidence about EXPO's applicability and sensitivity, while the code link and plotting details improve reproducibility information. However, the new entropy variant is inconsistently specified: Section 4.3 includes entropy in the TD target, whereas Section 4.4 says it is turned off. These useful additions therefore support a limited overall improvement rather than a clearly substantial one.
